basic_info.name: cleanyourtv
basic_info.description: Debloat any Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi and get an Apple TV-style home.

content.readme: > Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon! It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get > to Netflix. Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages > and wrote a new launcher. Looks like an Apple TV now lol. > > [@gathint, 17 October 2026](https://x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102). The replies are where > most of the TV lists here came from. The repo was called tv-vibehack until the 19th; old links work. ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling: 1. **Back up** the list of installed packages and settings. 2. **Disable** the manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. 3. **Install** a small native launcher and make it the default home screen. **No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.** The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start You need a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV and a coding assistant with shell access. Suggested: Claude Code on [0G Private Computer](https://pc.0g.ai), one API key for 100+ models. [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) with an [Anthropic plan](https://claude.com/pricing), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) or [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) work too. | | | |---|---| | **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. basic_info.name: free-my-tv
basic_info.description: A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV. Open source, built with Claude Code. One button to undo.

content.readme:
# Free My TV **A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV, LG and Samsung TVs.** Trending picks from your own apps, the weather at a glance, and a look that follows the sunset.
Open source. Built with Claude Code. One button to undo. [**freemytv.io**](https://freemytv.io) · [Install](#install) · [LG TVs](#lg-tvs-webos) · [Samsung TVs](#samsung-tvs-tizen) · [Any TV](#any-tv) · [Make it yours](#make-it-yours)
## What you get - **No ads.** No sponsored rows, banners or autoplaying promos. Not one. - **Your apps, front and center.** The streaming apps you actually use, on a glass shelf. Pick them and their order right on the TV. - **Trending, not sponsored.** Three fresh picks every hour from what's trending this week and the latest releases, only from apps you already have. Movies and Shows get their own tabs. - **Weather and markets, one press away.** The hour-by-hour forecast, sunrise and sunset, and live crypto prices. - **Light by day, dark by night.** It follows your city's real sunset, the way your phone does. - **A screensaver to match.** Full-screen photos of the picks with a big glass clock. - **Fast.** 60 fps, every frame in 16.6 ms, on the TV's own chip. The home screen uses 96 MB of memory instead of 242 MB (−60%).
Measured on a 98″ TCL Google TV running Android 14. - **Set up on the TV.** Language, your city, temperature, theme, the weather and prices cards, which coins, and the apps on the shelf, in Free My TV's own settings. - **Safe.** No root. Nothing is uninstalled. One button brings back the factory home screen. ## Install About ten minutes. You need a Google TV or Android TV (Android 9 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. ### The easy way: Claude Code 1. **On the TV**, turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press *Android TV OS build* 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Write down the TV's IP address (Settings → Network & Internet). 2. **On your computer**, get the code: ```bash git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv ``` 3. **Open [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) in that folder** and say: > Install Free My TV on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon. It installs the tools it needs, builds the app and puts it on your TV. Swap in your TV's IP and your city. 4. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*, and accept the debugging prompt (tick *Always allow*). ### The manual way 1. **On the TV**, do step 1 above. 2. **Tools:** a JDK (17+), the Android SDK command-line tools (build-tools 34, platform android-34) and adb. On a Mac: ```bash brew install --cask temurin android-commandlinetools android-platform-tools sdkmanager "build-tools;34.0.0" "platforms;android-34" ``` On Linux, get OpenJDK 17, Android's command-line tools and adb from your package manager, then run the same `sdkmanager` line. On Windows, use WSL. 3. **Build:** ```bash ./build.sh ``` The first run creates `config.properties`. Set your city and your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key) there, then run it again. 4. **Install:** ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.50:5555 adb install -r FreeMyTV.apk ``` On TCL TVs, also let it run in the background (TCL blocks it by default, and the switch never starts): ```bash adb shell "appops set io.freemytv AUTO_START allow || appops set io.freemytv APP_AUTO_START allow" ``` 5. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. ## LG TVs (webOS) The same home screen as an LG app: the picks, the glass shelf with your apps, the drawer with inputs, weather and prices, day and night, Home Settings and the shelf editor. It installs through LG's own Developer Mode, with nothing rooted or changed on the TV. LG's home screen stays where it is, and Free My TV is one press of a number key away. You need an LG TV (webOS 3 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi, with Python 3. 1. **On the TV**, open the LG Content Store and install **Developer Mode**. Sign in with a free [LG developer account](https://webostv.developer.lge.com), turn on **Dev Mode Status** (the TV restarts), then turn on **Key Server**. Write down the IP address and the passphrase it shows. 2. **On your computer**, get the code and build. `config.properties` works as for Google TV (your city, your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key)): ```bash git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv python3 webos/build.py ``` 3. **Install.** The first time, it asks for the TV's passphrase; updates don't: ```bash python3 webos/install.py 192.168.1.50 ``` 4. **On the TV**, while Free My TV is open, hold a number key on the remote. # AgentCraft **A team of Claude agents doing real work on your code, inside a Minecraft studio you can walk around in.** *Powered by Claude* [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-c9a227)](LICENSE) [![Minecraft 26.3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Minecraft-26.3-8fa98b)](https://www.minecraft.net) [![Fabric](https://img.shields.io/badge/mod%20loader-Fabric-d97757)](https://fabricmc.net) [![Claude Agent SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/agents-Claude%20Agent%20SDK-2fa3a0)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-548%20passing-3b2a20)](foreman/test)

Multi-agent coding usually means a wall of terminal text. AgentCraft turns it into a place. You type a goal. A lead agent reads your repo, writes a plan and pins tasks to a wall. Workers walk to their desks, sit down and start coding in their own git worktrees while their monitors stream every file they read and every line they change. When a call is genuinely yours, an agent walks over to you with a question. When work is ready, you review the real diff and press **Merge**. Nothing touches your branch without that click, and nothing is ever pushed. Close the game and the agents keep working. Open it again and the studio catches up.
## How a goal plays out
**1. You give a goal.** Press ` and type it. `@juniper` messages a specific agent, with Tab completion. **2. The lead plans.** Marlow splits the goal into tasks with dependencies. They land on the Task Wall, and the plan goes into the shared library.
**3. The team builds.** Each worker codes in its own worktree. Monitors stream the live log: tool calls, test runs, red and green diffs. **4. They come to you.** A clay ! appears, the bell rings, the agent walks to the podium. Press J to answer.
**5. You review and merge.** A real code review screen: file list, line numbers, collapsed context, the worker's summary and the reviewer's notes. **6. Memory stays shared.** The lead's plan, decisions and repo conventions live in a library every agent reads, and you can too.

## Meet the team Six hand-pixelled characters, each with their own silhouette and colour. **Marlow** leads: he plans, splits work and reviews. **Juniper, Kit, Wren, Rowan and Tove** build. They walk the studio with real pathfinding, sit at their desks while they type, show what they are doing with small particles and nameplates, talk in speech bubbles, and come find you when they need a decision.
## The studio
The Goal Atrium. Progress ring, task counts, and how many decisions need you. The studio floor. Desks, status lamps, the library and the lounge.
Everything is information you can read at a glance. Far away, the lamps and the cupola beacon tell you who is working, who is stuck and who is waiting on you. Closer, nameplates and cards tell you what. Up close, monitors and screens tell you exactly how.
## Proven with real agents This is not a mockup. These screenshots come from a real run with Claude agents on a sample repo, driven entirely through the game: a goal typed into the console, questions and permission prompts answered in game, merges reviewed in the diff screen, including a merge conflict sent back to the worker and resolved. The game was restarted mid run and the Foreman was taken offline and brought back. Six features landed in the repo with its tests passing.

Apple Watch Companion

Android · macOS · Linux · Windows
Native protocols. Physical hardware. A shared Companion.
Bluetooth · Pairing · IDS · Native Faces · Flutter · Java · Rust

     

Start here · Call map · Pairing · API · Build · Evidence

--- ## English

⚠️ TESTED ONLY ON watchOS 26.2 (23S303)

**Android Magisk module:** [Download Bridge 0.2.427 ZIP](https://github.com/LordixDemon/apple_watch_connector/releases/download/magisk-0.2.427/apple-watch-bridge-magisk-0.2.427.zip) · [Installation](#en-android-install) **Connect Apple Watch to Android, Linux and Windows through native Bluetooth/IDS protocols and a shared Flutter Companion. macOS uses the same interface with a limited Bluetooth backend.** This project reconstructs the path from discovery and pairing to activation, reconnection, preference exchange, and native watch-face management. Companion presents observed Watch state and submits commands on all four platforms. Android Bridge owns the phone connection and keys. Linux and Windows use a Rust desktop backend, native HCI brokers and the shared Java protocol engine; macOS uses Rust and CoreBluetooth. Linux and Windows pairing uses the six-digit Watch code; camera pairing is available on Android. Release preparation now has a shared Java `protocol-runtime` module, isolated research/debug probes, Linux artifact auditing and shared Android distribution signing. See the [release guide](docs/BUILD_AND_RELEASE.md). Fresh pairing, activation and same-pair encrypted reconnect are physically verified on Linux and Windows with the tested hardware; desktop application service coverage remains partial. The Linux Rust backend separates observed state, worker I/O/lifetime and command routing. Stop/failure states reject late ready events; EOF and bounded cleanup prevent stale readiness and abandoned workers. Portable Java modules share strict dependency locks. Linux packages include a verified schema-2 inventory and use deterministic archive metadata. See [stage 93](docs/REFACTOR_RELEASE_93.md). Linux now exposes Bluetooth adapter selection in All Watches, remembers the address across HCI index changes and requires reselection when saved hardware is missing. See [adapter selection](docs/LINUX_ADAPTER_SELECTION_94.md). > **Documentation snapshot: October 13, 2026.** The main verified hardware is Apple Watch Ultra 2, `Watch7,5`, watchOS `26.2 / 23S303`. Source versions: Bridge **0.2.429 / code 629**, Companion **1.0.86+87**, Rust workspace **0.1.1**. Source versions do not establish installed device versions. Android camera pairing, Linux pairing on Mint 22.3 and Windows pairing on Windows 10 / Realtek `0bda:b00e` have separate hardware verification. Development is ongoing. The hardware journal confirms camera pairing, activation, and a visible Watch face. Full Watch.app parity, every iPhone feature, and compatibility with every Apple Watch model remain incomplete. macOS discovery is implemented; the complete physical pairing → activation → IDS path is unfinished. ## Contents - [Capabilities and verification boundaries](#en-status) - [Project layout](#en-layout) - [System architecture](#en-architecture) - [End-to-end call map](#en-calls) - [Protocol stack](#en-stack) - [Fresh pairing, step by step](#en-pairing) - [Activation and Setup completion](#en-setup) - [Operational reconnection](#en-reconnect) - [Complete Companion → Bridge API registry](#en-api) - [IDS routes and handlers](#en-routes) - [Native faces: read, mutate, import, resources](#en-faces) - [Settings, pigments, and monograms](#en-preferences) - [Notifications, finding devices, Wi-Fi, and Health](#en-features) - [Modern StateReplicator and QUIC](#en-replicator) - [Keys, storage, and ownership](#en-ownership) - [Start from a clean machine](#en-start) - [Build, test, and first run](#en-build) - [macOS discovery build](#en-macos) - [Linux connection and adapter selection](#en-linux) - [Windows connection](#en-windows) -

basic_info.name: mcopt
basic_info.description: mcopt, a Minecraft mod: a native Metal renderer for Minecraft: Java Edition on Apple Silicon Macs (alpha)

content.readme:
# mcopt

> [!NOTE]
> mcopt no longer requires Sodium 🎉

A Minecraft performance mod for Apple Silicon Macs. Since 0.3.0-alpha.1 it draws the world with its own Metal renderer.
**Very much alpha:** expect bugs, and back up your worlds.

## Requirements

- An Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 26 or later
- Java 25 (the official launcher and Prism download it for 26.3; nothing to install)
- Minecraft 26.3 with Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer

## Install

1. Install Fabric for Minecraft 26.3: https://fabricmc.net/use/installer/ (or in Prism Launcher: new instance, 26.3,
   loader Fabric).
2. Download the mcopt jar from [Releases](../../releases).
3. Put it in `~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/mods`. Create the `mods` folder if it's missing
   (Finder: Go > Go to Folder). In Prism: Edit the instance > Mods > Add file.
4. Start Minecraft with the Fabric profile.

Sodium isn't needed anymore: mcopt won't start alongside it, so take Sodium out of that folder if it's there. Fabric API
isn't required; keep it if your other mods need it.

To check it's working: press F3 (fn + F3 on a Mac keyboard); the bottom right says `Metal 3 (mcopt)`.

Shows an fps counter in the top-left corner (hidden with F1 or F3; fn + F1 or fn + F3 on a Mac keyboard).

## Settings

- The perf profile is on by default.
- `profile=none` in `~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/config/mcopt.properties` (in Prism, the instance's
  `minecraft/config` folder) turns it off. The first launch writes that file.
- Far terrain is an experimental opt-in: `mcopt.lod=true` in the same file, for Macs with 10 or more GPU cores.

## Numbers

fps spinning / flying, same test world, 1920x1080, render distance 16, VSync off, at least two runs each:

| Mac | vanilla | Sodium 0.9.3 | 0.2.0-alpha.3 | 0.3.0-alpha.1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mac mini M4 (10-core GPU, 16 GB) | 156 / 146 | 275-281 / 253-267 | 1202-1223 / 1068-1074 | 1209-1211 / 1068-1069 |
| MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 5-core GPU, 8 GB) | 79-81 / 69-72 | 133-146 / 85-91 | 514-579 / 422-449 | 591-638 / 477-504 |
| Mac mini M6 (12-core GPU, 16 GB) | 297-328 / 283-291 | 454-460 / 406-413 | 1988-1991 / 1738-1742 | 2020-2022 / 1690-1704 |

The mini and Neo cells ran on 6c133ecc, whose only difference from 9865a0a3 is vGroup, which is gated off on those GPUs. The Neo's vanilla and Sodium cells come from the da566d00 run. This build differs from 9865a0a3 only in code that runs when Distant Horizons is installed.

For the most fps: Options > Video Settings, VSync off and Max Framerate Unlimited. The numbers above are with VSync off.

## Known issues

- Mods that require Sodium (for example Better Block Entities or Iris) can't be used with this build.
- Mods that call OpenGL directly can't draw on the Metal backend. To switch mcopt's renderer off, add
  `mcopt.metal=false` to `config/mcopt.properties` (or launch with `-Dmcopt.metal=false`).
- Distant Horizons runs on the Metal renderer next to mcopt's own terrain. With DH set to its OpenGL renderer, mcopt
  switches its renderer off for it.
- Far terrain is experimental. On Macs with fewer than 10 GPU cores, it costs most of the fps.

## Plans

- Far terrain on by default, with tiers for smaller Macs
- Our own shaders (BSL-level) as an option
- Faster world generation (native noise, bit-exact)
- More exact server-tick and chunk optimizations, held for later alphas
- Faster startup
- Wider hardware testing

## Licence and credits

[Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Keep the [NOTICE](NOTICE) file with any copy, and credit mcopt.

basic_info.name: AIKON
basic_info.description: A 2007 Nokia can't search Google anymore, so I gave it Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok. J2ME app for Nokia S40/S60 + tiny Go server.

content.readme: > **Formerly Claude S40.** The project was called *Claude S40* up to phone > app 0.10.x / server 0.7.x, while it only talked to Claude. Since it also > speaks to OpenAI, Gemini and Grok it is called **AIKON** (Nokia spelled > backwards). The repository moved from `emir/claude-s40` to `emir/AIKON` > (GitHub redirects the old address); the Java package and server names > keep the old name. ![AIKON: today's AI on a 2007 Nokia](docs/images/cover.png) **Today's AI on a 2007 Nokia.** AIKON is an AI chat client for Nokia Series 40 and Symbian S60 phones (Java ME, CLDC 1.1 / MIDP 2.0), plus the small Go server it talks to. Pick a model per chat (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini or Grok), type on the keypad, get the answer on a 240x320 screen: with today's news, weather and exchange rates from web search, long answers you can page through, and a UI in Turkish, English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Russian or Indonesian. Tested on the Nokia 6300 (S40) and the Nokia E63 (S60 QWERTY). **Video** (still as Claude S40): [on a Nokia 6300, on X](https://x.com/EmirKarsiyakali/status/2104183718483018026) ## Features **On the phone** - **Pick the model per chat**: first the provider (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Grok), then one of the models the server offers; switch in the middle of a chat with Options > Model. Every reply is labelled with its model. - **Chat**: your messages in bubbles, replies full width, day headings ("Today", "Yesterday"), and a typing indicator that counts the seconds. Replies keep their paragraphs and lists (dots, numbers, hanging indent); an unsent draft waits in the input bar. - **Web search** for news, weather, rates: the model searches on the server with its provider's search tool; the phone's 2007 browser is not involved. Sources are listed under the reply. - **Reading mode** (key 7): one reply full width, page by page, whole lines only, page number and progress line. It keeps its place when you change the text size (key 9) or load the rest. - **Long replies in parts**: "0 · Show the rest" fetches the next part from the server for free; the model is not asked again. - **Message actions**: select a message with 1/3, press the centre key: shorten, explain more simply, translate, ask about it, open it in the editor. They only fill in the editor; nothing is sent until you press Send. - **Earlier chats** from the server, continue any of them; **pin** the ones you want to keep at the top (kept until unpinned), **delete** or **search** all chats (no Turkish letters needed: "sise" finds "şişe"); optional offline copy of the last chat. - **Save to phone**: a reply as a .txt file (memory card if there is one), readable later without the network under "Saved". - **Calendar and to-do**: ask "add to my calendar: dentist tomorrow at 3" and the reply carries a ready entry; the centre key opens a prefilled form, and only your "Save" writes it to the phone's own calendar or to-do list. Works from any message too. - **Voice messages**: press Dictate, speak up to 30 seconds; the server turns it into text, which opens in the editor so you can check and fix it before you send it. - **Photos**: take one with the camera or pick one from the phone and ask about it ("what is this?", "translate this sign", "read this label"); follow-up questions in the same chat still see it. - **Your notes for the AI** (Settings): "I'm Emir, I live in Istanbul, keep it short" is sent with every message. - **Data usage**: requests and approximate kilobytes today and in total. - **20 quick prompts** (search the web, weather, translate, reply to a message, add to my calendar, summarize, fix my writing, ...). - **Short notes, details on request**: info and errors are one line; select one (1/3) and press the centre key for the explanation; setup and settings screens keep theirs under Options > Info. - **Setup wizard** on first start: server address, connection test, pairing with a 6-digit code (no long code to type); the language follows the phone. A build that names its server skips to the pairing. - **Keypad-first**: every screen works with the keypad (on QWERTY phones like the E63, the digits printed on the letter keys); a Shortcuts screen lists every key. Retry after an error is one key and never charges twice. - **Eight languages**: English, Türkçe, Español, Português, Français, Deutsch, Русский and Bahasa Indonesia. The app opens in the phone's language (English for any other) and changes under Settings > Language. The replies follow the language you write in, whatever the menus say. - **Look and feel**: every screen except text entry is drawn by the app: line icons with smooth edges, lists with two-line rows, settings with switches that save at once, full screen. Light, dark or automatic (dark in the evening) look, three text sizes, start-up animation and jingle, reply chime, vibration and ba

content.readme:
![Hushfacebook. Keep the people. Cut the noise.](assets/readme-hero.png)

# Hushfacebook Hushfacebook is a set of [Morphe](https://morphe.software) patches for the Facebook app on Android. You bring the Facebook APK, Morphe Manager patches it on your phone, and you get a Facebook with a settings screen of its own. Sponsored and suggested posts go away, and so do the ads in Stories, Reels, search and Marketplace. You can save reels, videos, stories and photos, open links in your own browser, hide the Reels tab and send Facebook less about what you do. Each row in the [patch table](#patches) says how its switch starts. The ad filters and a handful of others start on, and most of the rest start off until you turn them on. On a computer, [HushFacebook Web](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushFacebookWeb) is a separate userscript for Facebook in the browser. This project has no connection to Meta or to the Morphe project. Neither endorses it, and neither wrote it. The latest release is [v0.15.0](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/releases/tag/v0.15.0), with 93 patches. It includes all changes since v0.14.0, among them feed videos that open on their own, comments at full height or from a double tap, switches that hide the status bar, the Messenger button and the counts under posts and reels, settings in Simplified Chinese and a working Tap the bar to seek on 583, as the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) describes. [Add to Morphe](https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushfacebook) | [Download a release](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/releases/latest) | [Browse the patches](#patches) > [!IMPORTANT] > Back up your signing key after your first patch. Android only installs an update over your patched Facebook when it's signed with the same key, and without that key you'd have to uninstall, which deletes Facebook's data. [Keep your signing key](#keep-your-signing-key) shows how. ## Install 1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer. 2. Add Hushfacebook as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushfacebook 3. Download Facebook 583.0.0.39.55 from [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/facebook-2/facebook/). Take the bundle labelled (arm64-v8a) (480-640dpi) (Android 11+), build 475614366, which is a .apkm file. A phone with a 32-bit processor takes the (armeabi-v7a) (320dpi) (Android 11+) bundle, build 475614365, instead. 4. In Morphe Manager, tap **Select other apps**, then **Open APK file**, and pick that file. Android may ask for file access the first time. 5. Patch with the default selection and install. If Meta's own Facebook is on the phone, Android makes you uninstall it first, as [Package conflict](#package-conflict) explains. The default selection is every patch but three, so you don't need Expert mode. To add `AMOLED black theme`, `Material You theme` or `Disable Play Store updates`, turn on **Settings → Advanced → Expert mode** in Manager before you open the file, then pick them on the **Hushfacebook** tab. If you saved an Expert mode selection before, Manager keeps using it, so tap **Enable recommended patches** once to pick up the patches that joined the default selection since. If you also use another Facebook patch source, check that the two don't patch the same thing ([Patching stops on one patch](#patching-stops-on-one-patch)). ### Keep your signing key Morphe Manager signs the patched Facebook with a key it makes on your phone, and every update has to carry that same key. Back it up right after your first patch, under **Settings → System → Import & export → Signing key** in Manager, then tap **Export**. The button only shows up once you've patched something. Keep the `Morphe.keystore` file somewhere private, because anyone who has it can sign an APK your phone will take as an update. On a new phone, import the key in the same place before you patch anything. Reinstalling Manager or clearing its storage makes a new key, and Morphe's settings backup doesn't include it. With a different key, the only way forward is to uninstall the patched Facebook, which deletes its data. A Root Mount install sits over

content.readme:
# tv-home

**Make a slow, ad-filled Android TV fast and clean again.** Debloat it over Wi-Fi and give it a
tiny Apple TV-style home screen with rotating nature wallpapers. You can hand the whole thing to
Claude Code with one prompt, or do it by hand with the scripts here.

![Before: Google TV home with a sponsored hero. After: clean dock over a Lake Louise wallpaper](before-after.png)

On a 2 GB TCL Google TV this disabled 25 bloat apps and cut the home screen's memory use from
192 MB to 83 MB. Everything is reversible: packages are disabled, never uninstalled.

## Do it with Claude Code (easiest)

1. On the TV: Settings → System → About → press OK on **Build** 7 times → back → Developer options
   → turn on **USB debugging**. Keep the TV on, on the same Wi-Fi as your computer.
2. Clone this repo, open Claude Code inside it (so it can reuse the launcher and scripts), and paste:

   ```text
   My Android TV is slow and full of ads. Find it on my Wi-Fi, connect over ADB, and debloat it:
   disable the manufacturer's ads, telemetry and junk (reversibly, never uninstall), asking me first
   about apps and features I might use. Then build and install a fast, minimal Apple TV-style home
   screen with a dock of my favourite apps and rotating nature wallpapers. Back up before changing
   anything, check every step with screenshots from the TV, and give me a restore script.

   Heads-up from people who've done this: use the adb-shell Python package if macOS blocks adb; on
   Google TV also disable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith or it hijacks the Home button; and
   test the Home button from inside an app.
   ```

3. Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV when asked, then answer a few questions: which apps you
   use, which go in the dock, whether you want wallpapers.

The prompt is short on purpose; Claude works out the details. The gotchas below are there in case it gets stuck.

## Do it by hand (macOS)

```bash
./setup.sh                                                  # Python ADB client, JDK 17, Android SDK
tools/find-tv.sh                                            # finds the TV, saves its IP
tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe                # model, Android version
tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-google-tv-g07/debloat.txt     # or your own list, see examples/
launcher/build-and-install.sh                               # build + install the launcher
```

Undo everything with `tools/restore.sh <the same list>`.

## What's here

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md) | The prompt for Claude Code / any coding agent |
| [launcher/](launcher/) | The home screen. 4.7 MB including the wallpapers; plain Android, no network, no background services |
| [launcher/res/values/config.xml](launcher/res/values/config.xml) | Dock apps, hidden apps, Live TV app, grid columns |
| [tools/tv.py](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, screenshots, chunked APK push |
| [tools/find-tv.sh](tools/find-tv.sh) | Finds Android TVs on your Wi-Fi |
| [tools/type.sh](tools/type.sh) | Type into the TV's on-screen keyboard from your laptop (`tools/type.sh` alone prompts hidden, for passwords) |
| [tools/disable.sh](tools/disable.sh), [tools/restore.sh](tools/restore.sh) | Apply / undo a debloat list |
| [examples/](examples/) | Debloat lists per TV model |

## The launcher

- Clock, greeting and date top-left. Frosted pills top-right for **Inputs** (HDMI/AV/Live TV
  dropdown; the remote's Menu key opens it too), **Wi-Fi** (shows the network name) and **Settings**.
- A dock of your favourite apps. The focused app's name appears above it over a glow coloured from
  its banner. Press Down for every other app in a grid.
- 12 nature photos crossfade every 10 minutes, with a scrim so text stays readable. Swap them in
  `launcher/assets/wallpapers/` (1920×1080 JPEGs, credits in `launcher/WALLPAPER-CREDITS.md`).
- Deterministic D-pad focus, remembers the last tile, picks up newly installed apps on return.

Change the dock: edit `config.xml`, then run `launcher/build-and-install.sh`.

## Gotchas we hit

- **macOS blocks the `adb` binary** on the local network ("No route to host"). `tools/tv.py` uses
  the `adb-shell` Python package instead.
- **Google TV hijacks the Home button.** With the stock launcher disabled, the setup app
  (`com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith`) has a higher HOME priority than any third-party
  launcher. The install script disables it; `restore.sh` re-enables it.
- **Home opened the launcher behind the current app**, because of a stale home task from switching
  launchers. Force-stopping the launcher and `com.android.tv.settings` and pressing Home fixes it.
  The install script does this.
- **Chained `pm` commands** (`pm disable a; pm disable b`) can silently stop after the first. The
  scripts run one per shell call.
- **Apps installed from the Play Store didn't appear**, because the package broadcast was missed
  while another app was in front. The launcher re-checks wit

content.readme:
# tv-vibehack 📺✨

> **Transform any ad-bloated Android TV or Google TV into a lightning-fast, tvOS-inspired, fail-safe experience — without root, without bootloop risks, and without losing access to stock features.**

[![Android 14 Ready](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-14%20(API%2034)-green.svg)](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/14)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Root Required: No](https://img.shields.io/badge/Root-Not%20Required-brightgreen.svg)](#)
[![Zero Bootloop Architecture](https://img.shields.io/badge/Architecture-100%25%20Fail--Safe-orange.svg)](#the-100-fail-safe-architecture)

---

## 📐 Architecture & Transformation Overview

```text
[ STOCK GOOGLE TV ]                             [ NLRC TV VIBEHACK ]
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Sponsored Ad Banner (70% Screen)    │        │  NLRC Home · Ambient Clock & Date    │
│  [Trending Shows] [Paid Promotions]  │        │                                      │
│  50+ Bloatware OTT Apps              │   ➔    │                                      │
│  Remote Buttons Lock You In Paywalls │        │  Dock: [HDMI 2 (Cable)] [Media Vault]│
└──────────────────────────────────────┘        └──────────────────────────────────────┘
   • 2.5 GB RAM used                               • 120 MB RAM used
   • Heavy telemetry & tracking                    • 0 Ads · 0 Telemetry · 100% Fail-Safe
```

---

## 🎯 The Motivation

Modern Smart TVs ship with:
- **Sponsored ads covering 70% of the screen**.
- **Sluggish bloatware** and 50+ pre-installed background apps consuming memory and tracking habits.
- **Unremappable sponsored remote buttons** (Netflix, Prime Video) that elderly family members hit by mistake, throwing them into subscription walls.
- **Overly complicated navigation** that makes switching to Cable/HDMI or playing personal home videos a headache.

**tv-vibehack** solves this permanently. Originally built to give aging parents a distraction-free, one-touch TV experience, it provides a universal blueprint for taking back control of any Android TV without root.

---

## ⚡ What Makes This Different?

### 1. 🛡️ The 100% Fail-Safe Architecture (Zero Bootloops)
On Android 14 Google TV, disabling the stock launcher (`com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`) breaks Direct Boot, tripping Android's `RescueParty` service and bricking the TV into a black-screen recovery state.

**tv-vibehack never disables `launcherx`.** Instead:
- The custom launcher is **`directBootAware="true"`**.
- A lightweight native **Accessibility Service** (`HomeKeyService`) intercepts Home key events and window transitions in under 10ms.
- If the custom launcher is ever uninstalled or crashes, Google TV seamlessly takes over. **Zero chance of bricking your TV.**

### 2. 🔀 Hardware Passthrough (Direct HDMI Switching)
No more opening 4 nested TV menus just to watch cable. Through reverse-engineered Realtek RTD `TvContract` passthrough URIs, the launcher switches directly to HDMI inputs programmatically:
```java
Uri uri = TvContract.buildChannelUriForPassthroughInput(
    "com.realtek.tv.passthrough/.hdmiinput.HDMITvInputService/HW151519744" // HDMI 2
);
context.startActivity(new Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, uri));
```

### 3. 🎮 Sponsored Remote Key Remapping (No Root)
`HomeKeyService` intercepts hardcoded hardware remote buttons (`KEYCODE_BUTTON_3` for Netflix, `KEYCODE_BUTTON_4` for Prime Video, `KEYCODE_PROG_RED`/`GREEN`) and redirects them straight to HDMI 2 / Set-Top Box in <150ms without root.

### 4. 🎞️ Offline TV Media Vault & Legacy Transcoding
Many families have legacy home videos or recordings stored on USB drives encoded in older formats (e.g., DVD MPEG-2) that native modern Smart TV chipsets cannot decode inside standard MP4 containers.

#### How to Add Your Own Media:
1. **Transcode to Hardware-Accelerated H.264:**
   ```bash
   ffmpeg -i "MyVideo_Part_1.mp4" -c:v libx264 -preset faster -crf 23 -c:a aac -b:a 192k "Part_1.mp4"
   ```
2. **Push Directly into TV Internal Storage:**
   ```bash
   adb shell mkdir -p /sdcard/Movies/NLRC
   adb push Part_1.mp4 /sdcard/Movies/NLRC/Part_1.mp4
   adb push Part_2.mp4 /sdcard/Movies/NLRC/Part_2.mp4
   adb push Part_3.mp4 /sdcard/Movies/NLRC/Part_3.mp4
   ```
3. **Instant D-pad Remote Navigation:**
   Launch **PenDrive / Media Viewer** directly from the dock. No USB stick needs to remain plugged in; videos play natively at 60fps with intuitive remote controls:
   - ◄ / ►: Seek -10s / +10s with real-time HUD.
   - ▲ / ▼ or CH+ / CH-: Switch to Next / Previous part.
   - OK: Play / Pause toggle.

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Enable ADB on your Android TV
1. On the TV: **Settings** → **System** → **About** → Click **Build** 7 times to enable Developer Options.
2. Go to **Settings** → **System** → **Developer Options** → Turn on **USB Debugging** (and Network Debugging if available).
3. Connect your computer to the same Wi-Fi
